newsitem.title: USA: CME LIVE CATTLE FUTURES END MIXED, FEEDERS HIGHER.
newsitem.headline: CME LIVE CATTLE FUTURES END MIXED, FEEDERS HIGHER.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed mixed with nearby months weighed down by overbought conditions. Feeder cattle futures closed higher, largely influenced by a sharp slide in corn futures, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.750 cent per lb lower to 0.075 higher with August off most at 65.650 cents. Feeder cattle ended up 0.625 to 0.100 cent a lb with August up most at 80.800 cents.

Selling sparked by Friday's overbought status and ideas fed cattle prices will be steady at best this week, weighed on nearby live cattle. Showlists are up this week from last, partly due to a carryover of unsold cattle from last week.
Also, boxed beef trade slowed when prices rebounded slightly this morning after last week's skid, sources noted.
USDA quoted boxed beef cut-out values near midday up $0.16 to $0.31 per cwt, with 47 loads of fabricated cuts sold.
"The cash market is not inspiring any buying in the market, especially in the August contract," said Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp.
Levitt cited the large premium October is carrying over current cash levels which added to nervous selling.
October closed at 69.850 cents a lb versus sales last week in the cash market reported at $64.00 per cwt.
